news.originalContent:
The US president’s remarks come amid a deepening feud with Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Amid escalating tensions with Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy, United States President Donald Trump has increased pressure on the Eastern European country to make a deal that would end the war with Russia.

Speaking at the White House on Tuesday, Trump doubled down on his efforts to blame the Ukrainian president for holding up peace efforts that would bring the years-long conflict to a close.

“Zelenskyy has to want to settle this war, and if he doesn’t, I think it’s going to be a very bad thing,” Trump said as he talked about Russia having an “unlimited” supply of people to send in the fight.

Moments later, the US president referenced a contentious Oval Office meeting he held with Zelenskyy in February 2025, shortly after returning to power.

Zelenskyy, Trump said, could have made a “better deal” then. “He’s going to have to want to make a deal, because I don’t think his people are going to stand for it any longer,” Trump told reporters.

On Tuesday, the Ukrainian president met US special envoy Steve Witkoff and European leaders in Oslo, Norway, to discuss ending Russia’s war.

In a post on social media after the meeting concluded, Zelenskyy said, without providing specifics, that his country has “some clear ideas on how to get to peace”.

“We are united with our European partners in this effort, and we want the Americans to take these ideas to the Russians,” Zelenskyy wrote. “One of the important ideas is to move to a potential trilateral meeting of the leaders to address the issues that only the leaders can do.”

The Ukrainian leader added that Witkoff would head to Russia on Wednesday, where peace discussions are expected to continue.

“Let’s see what Putin has to say,” Zelenskyy said.

When asked whether Russian President Vladimir Putin should meet Zelenskyy, Trump said there was “tremendous” hatred between the two leaders.

“It’s hard for them to be in the same room,” Trump said. “I don’t care how it’s done.”

Trump’s remarks come as the White House continues to squeeze Ukraine in order to force the country to cut a deal with Russia.

Last week, Ukrainian officials reported slowdowns with Starshield, the military-grade version of the Starlink satellite system, run by the aerospace company SpaceX.

Ukraine relies on the technology for communications and intelligence to prevent Russian attacks.

It is unclear who ordered restrictions that limit Ukraine’s access to Starshield. SpaceX CEO and Trump ally Elon Musk pointed a finger at the White House.

“Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” he wrote on October 14.

The news agency Reuters also reported that the order came from inside the White House, citing two US officials and a Western official.

But a report in The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday claimed US officials had blamed Musk himself for the slowdown, saying the SpaceX CEO ordered it last week. Trump and US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth have both denied that the government directed the restrictions, with Hegseth pushing responsibility towards SpaceX.

Trump, meanwhile, has sought to ease the historically tense relations between Russia and the US.

In August 2025, Trump invited Putin to Alaska, the Russian leader’s first visit to US soil in a decade.

More recently, Trump has expressed openness this month to meeting with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, as part of a trilateral discussion on denuclearisation.

Trump also announced this month that he struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, marking a stunning reversal of years of US pressure on Moscow’s economy.

The US president also waived new economic restrictions that would have been imposed under the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a bipartisan law he signed one month earlier, in honour of a late senator.

It would have imposed sanctions on Russian officials, banks and tankers, as well as tariffs on countries that purchase Russian oil.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the decision on Tuesday, saying the law allowed the waiver through a provision embedded in the legislation.

“The president chose to use a national security waiver to not immediately implement those [sanctions and restrictions], because he recognises that these things have to be looked at in their totality,” Rubio said in an interview with India’s News18.

Rubio argued that Trump was engaged in a “balancing act” in deciding the extent of US-imposed economic restrictions and how they could impact the rest of the world.

“When you do that pressure, sometimes it spills over and has a negative impact on other countries,” Rubio said.

A California native tribe is standing their ground.

Members of Northern California’s Wailaki tribe say plans for the Great Redwood Trail — a 307-mile nature trail stretching from from the San Francisco Bay to Humboldt Bay, would allow tourists to walk right over the graves of their ancestors.

The project, which is 40% complete, was exempted from from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), which requires public agencies to notify and consult native tribes about projects that impact them, further upsetting the local tribe.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Wailkai tribe member Perry Lincoln says that when locals first heard of the trail a few years ago, after plans were well underway, they felt blindsided.

“You’re just kind of shoving it down our throats,” he told the LA Times.

The scenic trail is being built along the long-defunct Northwestern Pacific Railroad and the Eel River. State Sen. Mike McGuire has shown support for the trail.

“What this trail will do is open up some of the most spectacular landscapes on Earth,” McGuire told the LA Times. “Folks will be able to traverse past giant ancient redwoods to mighty rivers … through lush vineyards, golden rolling hills.”

Some environmental groups also support the trail, saying it will have a positive environmental impact on the area.

“It just is basically infeasible to imagine that this scale of restoration could happen” without the state handling it, Alicia Hamann, executive director of the nonprofit Friends of the Eel River told the newspaper.

The Pacific Northwestern Railroad closed in 1998 after severe El Niño storms impacted the railroad. After years of talk about a possible trail along the defunct railway, the Great Redwood Trail Agency, which controls the land along the railway, was created in 2021.

More than 1 million people walked, hiked or biked the southern segment of the trail last year, according to McGuire.

“I’m a big advocate for rail trails,” Bruce Silvey of the Humboldt Trails Council told the LA Times.. “They’re beautiful and they’re fun and they’re easy to ride. You can do 30 miles because they’re basically flat.”But not all officials are thrilled about the project. Steve Madrone, a Humboldt County supervisor, left the trail agency earlier this year, partly because of the project’s exemption from CEQA review.

“Think about the trauma that these tribes have experienced,” he told the LA Times. “That did not help remove that mistrust. It reinforced that mistrust.”

But ultimately, Madrone supports the trail, believing it will bring business to small towns along the route.

Elaine Hogan, executive director of the Great Redwood Trail Agency, told the LA Times that attempts to contact the tribe have been made, but Lincoln says he nor any tribe member he knows has heard anything.

The tribe, who do not live on their ancestral land, say they rarely have access to it themselves.

“We’re barely getting access to these areas ourselves, but we’re going to allow outside communities to have full access to these places?” Lincoln’s daughter Tisanche Warren told the LA Times. “That doesn’t seem fair.”

The NFL betting landscape looks dramatically different just one-third into the season.

From a new Super Bowl favorite to a stunning injury-driven collapse and a surprise leader in the Rookie of the Year race, oddsmakers have been busy adjusting their forecasts.

Here are four of the biggest betting trends heading into Week 7.

The 49ers are the new team to beat in the Super Bowl futures market.

San Francisco improved to 6-0 with Monday’s win over Washington, moving from +680 to +540 at DraftKings Sportsbook.

Meanwhile, the Rams’ disastrous start continues to take a toll on their championship hopes.

Los Angeles, which entered the season as the Super Bowl favorite, dropped to 2-4 after Sunday’s shocking loss to the Cardinals as 12.5-point favorites.

The Rams have plummeted from +700 to 12/1 in just one week.

Philadelphia’s season has gone from bad to worse.

The Eagles have lost four straight games, and the news that Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the season due to blood clots has sent their Super Bowl odds tumbling from 40/1 to 200/1 at DraftKings.

The fallout has extended to the point-spread market.

Philadelphia opened as a 3-point favorite against Dallas on Monday night but is now a 5.5-point home underdog — a staggering 8.5-point swing.

Kansas City has yet to lose a game this season, but oddsmakers apparently aren’t convinced.

Despite their 5-0 record, the Chiefs are 2.5-point underdogs against the defending champion Seahawks on Sunday night.

Seattle has dropped two straight games and is just 1-3-2 against the spread this season.

The Seahawks opened as 1.5-point favorites, but the line has moved another point in their favor.

It’s the first time Patrick Mahomes and Co. have been underdogs this season.

The Offensive Rookie of the Year market has a new favorite.

Titans wide receiver Carnell Tate has surged to +200 at DraftKings, overtaking Denzel Boston, who led the pack just last week.

Tate caught six passes for 70 yards and his first NFL touchdown Sunday against the Colts, bringing his season totals to 29 receptions and 344 yards.

He was listed at +500 last week.

Jeremiyah Love (+300) and Boston (+400) remain his closest competition in an increasingly competitive awards race.

Dylan Svoboda is a versatile writer and analyst across many sports. He’s particularly knowledgeable about the big three — MLB, the NFL and the NBA.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

State Attorney General Letitia James dropped the ball on protecting New Yorkers, a group of crime victims and their relatives said Tuesday as they rallied for GOP challenger Sarita Komatireddy.

Komatireddy, a former federal prosecutor, vowed to give victims and their families a “direct line” to the attorney general’s office if she’s elected next month.

“In New York today, the reality is, criminals have more of an audience with our elected officials than crime victims,” Komatireddy said during a press conference outside James’ Lower Manhattan office.

Six New Yorkers impacted by violence and drugs gathered with the Republican candidate, ripping the Empire State’s lax criminal justice laws backed by Democrats including two-term incumbent James and Gov. Kathy Hochul.

“They’re all angry,” Komatireddy said. “They’re all tired of being ignored. Each one of them is a victim of lawlessness.

“For the first time… those victims will have a direct line to the attorney general,” Komatireddy said — as she unveiled her plan to establish a “Victims Advisory Council” within the AG’s Office if she unseats James on November 3.

Among those standing with Komatireddy was Tatiana Brahimi, a Putnam County mom whose 18-year-old son was struck and killed by a car during a 2016 Dutchess County brawl.

“I’m not a politician. This is why I believe in Saritha. She is not a politician,” Brahimi told reporters.

“Letitia James and all those cronies before her do not care about us. I buried a child. How many of us are burying our loved ones?  The government doesn’t care. We need people like Saritha, who cares.”

Madeline Brame lost two sons — Army veteran Sgt. Hason Correa, who was stabbed to death in Harlem in 2018, and Rayvon Brame, who overdosed on fentanyl-laced cocaine — and said she was backing Komatireddy because victims and their families “need a seat at the table.”

Long Island mom Teresa Bliss, whose son, 25-year-old David Bliss, was shot to death in broad daylight in Port Jefferson in 2021 by a career criminal on probation, said the system failed her family.

She recalled finding out that her son had been killed through the radio — after authorities told her to wait in her car outside a local police precinct when she went there searching for David.

“These cascading failures — from the judicial disposition of probation, in lieu of  incarceration, to lax probation enforcement, to the absence of proper, dignified family notification protocols — demonstrate a complete system breakdown,” Teresa Bliss said.

“This is exactly why victims and surviving families need a permanent voice,” she said. “Because after the most painful, life altering nightmare of our lives, we are asking for one simple thing: to be heard.”

New York’s 2019 criminal justice reforms bar judges from setting bail on most crimes, letting more offenders roaming the streets and in some cases committing new crimes.

“In Kathy Hochul and Letitia James in New York, we’ve seen the consequences of criminal justice policies that, in my view, far too often put offenders ahead of the victims,” said Jennifer Harrison, a Long Islander who founded Victims Rights NY after her boyfriend was murdered outside a New Jersey nightclub in 2005.

“When the criminal justice system fails a victim, where are we supposed to go if not for people like Saritha?” she said.

“We have activist judges, prosecutors whose decisions raise serious questions about public safety, bail reform, a parole board that families believe too often disregards the severity of violent crime, and failures to enforce parole and probation violations,” she added.

But Komatireddy accused James of also not doing enough for the victims, and said her advisory council will give them a voice in shaping office’s public safety and enforcement priorities.

“We will place victims at the center of what we do, and give them the respect and dignity that they deserve,” she said.

In an interview with the independent journalist group The New York Editorial Board, Komatireddy said she would send prosecutors from the AG’s to local district attorneys’ offices when victims raise complaints that their cases are falling through the cracks.

“We need to make sure that there is an open line of communication with crime victims. [That] if a crime victim is dissatisfied with their local DA, that they have someone to call,” she said in the interview published on Substack — also vowing she would re-dedicate half of the AG’s Office’s 700 prosecutors to criminal cases.

Jennifer Driver, the mother of Sarah Patricia Goode, a 21-year-old Long Island woman who was raped and murdered after rejecting a creep‘s sexual advances in 2014, said it’s sorely needed.

“Victims and survivors deserve a permanent voice in the laws, policies, and services that affect their lives,” Driver said. “It would help turn our pain into purpose and ensure victims are treated with dignity, compassion, and the support they deserve.

“Not an afterthought,” she said. “We cannot change what happened to our loved ones, but we can work to improve the system so that future victims and their families are heard, supported, and treated with the respect that they deserve.”

Komatireddy, an underdog in the race, pulled within just six points of James in a recent Republican internal poll, which showed the incumbent with a narrow 50.7% to 44.7% edge.

Earlier this week, she blamed James for the subway “chaos” that saw the seventh transit homicide in the Big Apple so far this year, nearly double the four murders over the same span in 2025.

“Survivors deserve results, not politics,” a spokesperson for James said in a statement.

“Attorney General Letitia James has always fought for them, including suing the federal government to protect more than $212 million in services for survivors of violent crime,” the statement said. “While our opponent stages political events, Attorney General James is at work delivering for every New Yorker.”

A democratic socialist City Council member skipped another slate of government hearings to head upstate — after The Post reported he had the worst attendance record of any local lawmaker.

Chi Ossé, a Democratic Socialists of American chum of Mayor Zohran Mamdani, ditched government hearings on Monday and Tuesday to instead travel multiple hours outside of his Brooklyn district to head to Rochester and Syracuse.

The lefty council member, who had eyed then abandoned a primary run against US House of Representatives Democratic Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries last year, had announced that he’d attend a “rally” for lower electric bills on Monday — the same day The Post exposed his chronic absenteeism.

“New York I’m going on tour…to take over our utilities! It’s time to lower our energy bills and secure clean, renewable energy!,” he wrote in a post to X.

Ossé’s out-of-district tour saw him miss an oversight hearing of “CreateNYC” – the Big Apple’s first comprehensive cultural plan — and a pair of committee votes on an urban development project and a property tax exemption.

The office-allergic politician already missed four of the council’s 18 stated meetings in the 2025-2026 legislative sessions – the worst of any council member – and has only made it to 67.6% of his committee meetings, which makes him one of the six least engaged on the council.

Ossé brushed off The Post’s reporting on his lackluster attendance record in a post to X Tuesday — claiming his chronic case of absenteeism was due to his work fighting energy company Con Edison.

“I’ve been traveling across New York State fighting to take over ConEd to lower our energy bills! I promise I’ll be back soon XO,” he wrote.

Ossé’s upstate tour left one Democratic operative scratching their head.

“This guy hasn’t a clue what he’s talking about,” said the operative, who has lived in the Syracuse area for more than a decade.

“You can’t drive to Syracuse, meet a few people for a few minutes, put out a press release, and call that work. We call that cheap,” he said.

The Tuesday rally in Syracuse coined “Take Back Our Power” was set to feature Ossé, state Assembly member Sarahana Shrestha, and Onondaga County Legislator Mo Brown. It was sponsored by the Syracuse branch of the DSA.

“Respectfully, focus on the issues of the constituents in your district, one X user wrote,” in response to the rally flyer.

A spokesperson for Ossé and the City Council didn’t respond to a request for comment Tuesday.

Ossé brushed off The Post’s reporting on his lackluster attendance record in a post to X Tuesday — claiming his chronic case of absenteeism was due to his work fighting energy company Con Edison.

“I’ve been traveling across New York State fighting to take over ConEd to lower our energy bills! I promise I’ll be back soon XO,” he wrote.

Ossé’s upstate tour left one Democratic operative scratching their head.

“This guy hasn’t a clue what he’s talking about,” said the operative, who has lived in the Syracuse area for more than a decade.

“You can’t drive to Syracuse, meet a few people for a few minutes, put out a press release, and call that work. We call that cheap,” he said.

The Tuesday rally in Syracuse coined “Take Back Our Power” was set to feature Ossé, state Assembly member Sarahana Shrestha, and Onondaga County Legislator Mo Brown. It was sponsored by the Syracuse branch of the DSA.

“Respectfully, focus on the issues of the constituents in your district, one X user wrote,” in response to the rally flyer.

A spokesperson for Ossé and the City Council didn’t respond to a request for comment Tuesday.

It has been, remarkably, 23 years since the last Knicks jersey was retired at Madison Square Garden.

Since James Dolan took over these types of decisions, No. 33 is also the only Knicks number retired, a no-brainer for Patrick Ewing, the franchise’s all-time leader in points, games, minutes, rebounds and blocked shots.

The standard is high in the Garden rafters, at least when it comes to the Knicks. The NBA Cup wasn’t prestigious enough to get a banner until Tuesday, nearly a full year after the Knicks won Adam Silver’s beloved tournament. Bernard King, John Starks and Carmelo Anthony aren’t up there. If Melo’s jersey is retired, the bar is lowered and there should be calls for retroactive enshrinements. But Melo’s not up there. Thankfully. He had great moments but is not deserving of a retired jersey. It’s only No. 33 for Ewing, No. 15 for Dick McGuire and a lot of champions — the combined starting lineups of 1970 and 1973, plus the coach:

No. 10 Walt Frazier, No. 19 Willis Reed, No. 12 Dick Barnett, No. 22 Dave DeBusschere, No. 24 Bill Bradley, No. 613 for Red Holzman’s career victories.

A Minnesota rapper who traveled to France to join escalating riots has urged white people to “raise hell” and “f*** s*** up” as part of a revolution on American soil, The Post discovered. And communist-linked groups in the US may be working to bring that hell to the nation’s capital.

Artist Tufawon, whose real name is Rafael Gonzalez Jr., joined Swedish activist Greta Thunberg outside Paul Éluard, the high school at the heart of the leftist protests marred by violence, looting and arson.

He addressed balaclava-clad protesters before performing his song “No One Is Illegal,” and riling up the crowd with chants of “f*** ICE” and “ICE out.”

“All power to the people,” the 40-year-old from Minneapolis boasted to his fans on Facebook. “After returning home from France I can clearly see how we need to become far more radicalized in the states.

“We have to be more enraged. Our comfort is hindering our progress. It really and truly needs to be white people that go outside and raise hell if we want to see revolution.

“There are far too many neoliberals that are just as bad as the fascists. The French have figured this out a while ago. Now it’s time to take it to the next level. Go f*** s*** up white people. It’s your time.”

“They said they were going to globalize the intifada and now they have,” foreign policy expert at the Heritage Foundation Mike Gonzalez told The Post.

“What you are seeing here is the red-green alliance, the marriage of convenience between leftists and Marxists. They have a common enemy which is the Judeo-Christian democratic West. They want to dismantle it.”

Tufawon, who is part Native American and has appeared on the popular radio show The Breakfast Club, claimed that the perceived underfunding of schools and declining public services in France is similar in the US.

“I’m incredibly inspired by what’s going on with the student activists and organizers,” the rapper said.

“The most marginalized students, the brown and the black students are the ones that are feeling the implications the worst.”

Tufawon urged fellow protesters in the US to “take influence from the French” so that they can defeat the “same common enemy”.

“It is dangerous rhetoric,” Gonzalez told The Post. “If people listen to him and act upon what he is recommending it is very dangerous.”

The rioters have targeted France’s cultural heritage, with thugs torching the 140-year-old city hall in the southern city of Limoges, and some have hit stores including Louis Vuitton, Hermes, and Apple as French authorities appeared to lose control of the streets.

Meanwhile, CCP-linked nonprofit Code Pink, backed by Neville Singham, has wasted no time using the unrest in France to plan similar protests in America, with a “taxpayer uprising” planned in Washington, DC, between November 10 and 12.

The feminist anti-American group has called on protestors to flood the halls of Congress in what it calls “three days of peaceful resistance.”

But its leader Jodie Evans, 72, a radical Hollywood filmmaker and wife of Shanghai-based tech millionaire Singham, called on “people to look at France” as she urged Americans to take to the streets.

CodePink has been accused of radicalizing a new generation of activists by spending millions of dollars to teach anti-American rhetoric.

Elsewhere, the Singham-linked Party for Socialism and Liberation, based in the US, has committed to joining French protesters in their “struggle for a socialist future”.

“We in the United States stand with you in your struggle against capitalist austerity,” the group proudly wrote on Instagram.

“We stand with you, because we too demand money for housing and education, instead of war and occupation. Vive la commune! Vive la révolution!”

Gonzalez, who fled communist Cuba in the 1970s, insists that China, Cuba and Iran are directing these protests. “These activists are taught to despise their own society,” he told The Post. “The groups involved in elevating the French protests, a lot are in the Singham network.”

Police made 2,500 arrests across France, while nearly 1,000 officers were injured over the weekend.

French President Macron said that “nothing justifies” the riots his country has seen and blamed the “unrestrained violence” on “insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals.”

His comments came after Vice President JD Vance blamed mass immigration for the violent scenes in France.

“Western liberals imported the Third World into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this, and they didn’t listen,” he wrote on X.

“I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn,” Vance added.

Tufawon, CodePink and the Party for Socialism and Liberation declined to comment.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Boeing’s 737 Max 10 airliner has been approved for passenger service after years of delays, the Federal Aviation Administration announced Tuesday.

The Max 10’s certification represents another milestone in Boeing’s efforts to restore its reputation and financial footing after years of safety, quality and production challenges. With production approved, the aircraft can now be sold to domestic and foreign carriers.

“After extensive safety reviews – including thousands of hours of test flights – the team at the FAA is ready to approve this critical aircraft for sale,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a statement.

“This is a major win for American manufacturing and our nation’s status as a global aviation powerhouse.”

Duffy is expected to speak about the decision later Tuesday during a visit to Boeing’s manufacturing plant in Everett, Washington.

The Max 10 is an important piece of Boeing’s effort to regain ground in the narrow-body market.

For airlines, the larger plane offers a way to carry more passengers on a single flight, potentially lowering costs per seat.

For travelers, it could eventually mean more seats on popular routes, though the impact on fares will depend on how airlines deploy the planes and how much competition they face.

The single-aisle jet, which can have up to 230 seats, was introduced at the Paris air show in 2017 to help Boeing compete with rival Airbus.

But technical and regulatory hurdles repeatedly delayed certification of the largest version of Boeing’s bestselling 737 family.

Boeing said in its 2020 annual report that it expected to make the plane’s first delivery in 2023.

The company now expects to begin deliveries in 2027.

The delays have held up a key part of Boeing’s business.

Speaking at an investors conference last month, CEO Kelly Ortberg said the Max 10 accounted for roughly 30% of Boeing’s 737 backlog.

The company’s website lists its total 737 backlog at more than 4,500 aircraft.

The Max 10’s certification completes the lineup of four 737 Max models.

The FAA cleared the smaller Max 7 for airline operations in August.

Boeing’s struggles have been particularly acute since two deadly crashes involving the smaller Max 8 killed 346 people in 2018 and 2019 off the coast of Indonesia and in Ethiopia.

In 2024, a panel flew off of an Alaska Airlines Max 9 in midair, renewing scrutiny of Boeing’s manufacturing and safety practices.

The Max 10 is intended to compete with Airbus’s A321neo model family, which entered service in 2017. The largest A321neo can carry more passengers and fly farther without refueling than the Max 10.

Still, Boeing designed the Max 10 to carry more passengers while burning less fuel than older aircraft — a potentially attractive combination for airlines facing soaring jet fuel costs amid the U.S. war with Iran.

Those rising costs have put added pressure on airlines to control expenses. Certification means the FAA has determined that the Max 10’s design meets safety standards, following engineering reviews and flight testing.

But Boeing must continue to show it can consistently build the aircraft to the approved design, and each plane must be cleared before it can fly passengers.

In the wake of the fatal Max 8 crashes, the FAA overhauled how it certifies Boeing aircraft. But over the past 18 months, the agency has gradually eased some of its restrictions on the company, increasing the limit on how many planes Boeing can produce.

In July, the FAA also said Boeing could once again issue airworthiness certificates for its 737 Max and 787 planes at the end of production, allowing the company to take back some responsibility for determining whether finished aircraft are ready to fly.

Boeing’s Everett site offers additional flexibility because the Max 10 is longer than other variants of the 737 Max family.

Ortberg said the aircraft could not be arranged nose-to-tail on its production line in Renton, Washington, where Boeing builds the 737, but could be accommodated in Everett.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

That would allow Boeing to produce a greater mix of longer aircraft as it ramps up production, Ortberg said.

Major customers for the Max 10 include United Airlines, Delta Air Lines, American Airlines and Ryanair.

Alaska Airlines joined that list in January, ordering 105 Max 10s, with options for 35 more.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic booked a staggering $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of 2026 — mostly from accounting charges — as it warned that growing opposition to data centers could threaten its business.

The San Francisco-based company, which is preparing for a blockbuster IPO that could value it at as much as $2 trillion, voiced caution about the growing movement of anti-data center and anti-AI voters.

Resistance to data centers has “become more organized and coordinated across jurisdictions,” Anthropic said in the filing viewed by the Wall Street Journal.

The company, led by CEO Dario Amodei, said its high public profile “may draw particular attention to projects associated with us.”

Anthropic said most of its data center capacity is located in the US, although it has signed letters of intent to develop additional facilities overseas. Domestically, recent months have seen public opinion souring on AI and protests opposing data center construction.

Lior Prosor, a partner at Deep33 Ventures, downplayed the likelihood that the backlash would derail Anthropic’s IPO or impede its near-term growth.

“Risk the IPO? I don’t think so,” Prosor told The Post, explaining that data centers only now entering the permitting process wouldn’t be operational before the second half of 2028.

He nevertheless acknowledged that regulatory obstacles could become a more serious problem over the long term.

Anthropic said it has sought more computing capacity than its major cloud partners were willing to provide.

The company faces more than $600 billion in future cloud computing and chip-leasing costs, with deals under negotiation that could add another $150 billion, the Journal reported.

Prosor said Anthropic is “certainly taking meaningful risks” with its enormous computing commitments, even as surging demand for artificial intelligence has rewarded companies that secured capacity early.

He argued that Anthropic should “raise as much capital as possible” to weather potential setbacks as the market matures.

“This is not going to be straight up and to the right forever,” Prosor warned.

The first-half loss, up from $13 billion a year earlier, included roughly $72 billion in accounting charges tied to changes in the value of convertible notes and other financing instruments, according to the report.

The $72 billion reflected changes in the value of convertible notes and other fundraising instruments.

Meanwhile, the siblings running Anthropic earned less in total compensation last year than the median CEO of an S&P 500 technology company, according to pay data cited by the Journal.

Dario Amodei and his sister, company president Daniela Amodei, each drew a base salary of roughly $655,000 in 2025.

But the siblings aren’t exactly struggling.

Stock and option awards boosted Dario’s total compensation to about $18 million last year, while Daniela’s pay package was valued at roughly $16.5 million, according to the filing.

Their pay packages were roughly in line with median CEO compensation across the S&P 500, but fell short of the median for the index’s technology companies, according to MyLogIQ data cited by the Journal.

The siblings could also receive more equity if certain milestones are reached, the draft prospectus shows.

Anthropic’s co-founders have each pledged 80% of their stakes to philanthropy, while the company separately plans to commit 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund announced Sunday.

Meanwhile, revenue surged to $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $1.1 billion a year earlier.

Over the same stretch, computing and infrastructure expenses jumped to nearly $9 billion from $2.3 billion.

Anthropic also warned that its business remains heavily dependent on a handful of large clients, with just two customers accounting for roughly one-fifth of its first-half revenue.

The company expects a “significant portion” of sales to continue coming from a “limited number of customers for the foreseeable future,” according to the prospectus.

Anthropic declined to comment to the Journal on the disclosures, which come as the AI giant prepares to tap public investors to help finance its ambitious expansion.

The Post has sought comment from Anthropic.

news.originalContent:
The lawsuit argues Trump bypassed Congress and misused a century-old law to impose sweeping tariffs on Canadian imports.

A US food importer is suing US President Donald Trump over his 50 percent tariffs on Canadian goods, arguing he lacks the legal authority to impose sweeping tariffs without congressional approval.

Gellert Global Group, a New Jersey-based company that imports Canadian cheese, filed the lawsuit on Tuesday in the US Court of International Trade in New York.

The company says the tariffs are driving up its costs and disrupting its relationships with suppliers on both sides of the border. Between September 16 and October 11, Gellert had paid more than $520,000 in duties, according to the complaint.

“Gellert Global Group has spent generations building trusted relationships with suppliers, customers and partners across the food industry,” said Thomas Gellert, the company’s co-chief executive officer, in a press release. “These tariffs disrupt those relationships overnight and create costs and uncertainty that ripple through the entire supply chain.”

The lawsuit challenges Trump’s decision to use a Depression-era law to impose tariffs on a wide range of Canadian products, including dairy products, furniture, clothing and wine.

Trump first imposed the 50 percent tariffs over the summer, accusing Canada of discriminating against American-made cars, alcohol and dairy products. He expanded the measures in September, adding more products in response to Canadian retaliatory tariffs.

The lawsuit argues that the law doesn’t apply to the Canadian policies the Trump administration says are discriminatory, since two of them “arose in response to the president’s own tariffs, while the third involves Canadian dairy policy governed by the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA)”.

It also questions why Canadian cheese is being taxed over disputes involving alcohol and cars.

“No president should have the power to pull a dormant statute off the shelf and use it to impose sweeping tariffs or import bans without the limits Congress required,” said Sara Albrecht, chairman and CEO of the Liberty Justice Center, a nonprofit legal organisation that filed the suit on Gellert’s behalf.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment, according to the Reuters news agency.

At the centre of the case is Section 338 of the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act of 1930, which allows the president to impose tariffs of up to 50 percent on imports from countries found to discriminate against American businesses.

The provision had never been used until Trump invoked it this year.

The lawsuit argues that newer laws passed by Congress since then, such as Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, require investigations, public comment and other safeguards that Gellert says the Trump administration has bypassed, and that these override Section 338.

“The administration cannot skip those protections by reaching for a 1930 statute that no president had ever used to impose a tariff,” said Jeffrey Schwab, the Liberty Justice Center’s senior counsel and director of litigation.

In addition, the lawsuit says that even if Trump is allowed to use the older law, he hasn’t met its requirements, including waiting 30 days before tariffs can be collected on new products added to the list.

The administration only waited seven days to start collecting tariffs on cheese in September, according to the lawsuit.

Gellert is asking the court to declare the tariffs illegal, stop them from being collected, and order refunds with interest for importers who have been impacted.

The lawsuit marks the fourth major legal challenge to Trump’s tariffs.

In February, the US Supreme Court struck down most of the tariffs he imposed in 2025, and a trade court later ruled against a temporary 10 percent global tariff. A separate challenge to tariffs imposed over alleged forced labour in international trade is still pending.

Republicans and Democrats jockey for control of Congress, which will set course for Trump’s final two years in office.

The United States midterms on November 3 are dominating national and international headlines.

The stakes of the election are high. The midterm race will determine which party controls the US Congress, and in turn, shape the direction of Trump’s final two years in office. It will also decide key state and local positions.

But notching big wins in the midterm election may not be enough to shake up the balance of power in Washington, DC.

To understand the implications of this year’s midterm election and what may come next, Al Jazeera has put together this simple primer.

Here’s why the US midterms matter at the federal level.

Midterm elections fall at the halfway point of a president’s term, meaning the executive office will not be on the ballot.

Front and centre will be the battle for control of Congress. Two chambers make up the US legislature: the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Because members of the House serve two-year terms, all 435 seats in the chamber are up for election on November 3. However, most races are already considered formalities, with a clear frontrunner.

That leaves only a handful of races — about 50 — to decide who will win the House majority.

While subject to change, nearly every reputable election prognosticator has predicted that Democrats will win control of the House, some by as many as 15 seats.

The Democrats have a slimmer chance of winning a majority in the Senate, however.

That chamber has only 100 seats. But because senators have staggered six-year terms, only 35 seats are up for election. Only about a dozen of those races are considered competitive.

Still, Democrats have seen their odds of seizing the Senate increase, as the number of competitive races has grown.

Left-wing candidates have made inroads in deep-red states like Texas and Kansas, creating more opportunities for the Democratic Party to claim a Senate majority this election cycle.

Because the US vice president breaks ties in the Senate, Democrats would need 51 seats to control the chamber.

Congress passes laws and approves federal budgets. But even if a party secures a majority in both chambers of Congress, it may not be enough to control the country’s legislative agenda.

Laws can pass by a simple majority in the House, but they typically need a supermajority of 60 votes in the Senate to overcome a process known as the filibuster. That process can allow a minority group to stall legislation indefinitely, barring a supermajority.

Therefore, unless a party wins more than 60 seats in the Senate, most legislation will still require at least some level of bipartisan support to pass.

Even if legislation passes both chambers, the president can veto any bill that comes across his desk. Overriding a presidential veto requires a two-thirds supermajority in both the House and the Senate.

Achieving the broad bipartisan support needed to overcome a presidential veto is exceedingly rare.

The last time it happened was in January 2021, during Trump’s first term. At the time, the US president had lost the 2020 election, and he saw his support from Republican lawmakers dissipate when he attempted to veto a defence spending bill.

Still, there are instances when bipartisan support overcomes presidential objections. A bill to increase the housing supply passed both the House and Senate with veto-proof majorities earlier this year, despite Trump’s stated opposition.

Republicans currently hold two majorities in Congress, with 53 seats in the Senate and 218 in the House.

With Trump in the White House, that means the party has held a so-called government “trifecta” over the last two years, with three levers of power under its command.

The Republican majorities in Congress have helped Trump pass some of his signature legislation, including surging funding to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and cleaving back some forms of publicly funded healthcare as part of a sweeping 2025 tax bill.

But Republicans’ numbers have not been enough to pass Trump’s entire legislative wishlist. Notably, he has been unable to pass his signature federal voter identification law, dubbed the “SAVE America Act“, amid Democratic opposition.

There have also been a handful of issues where Republicans have defied Trump, particularly on tariffs. A few Republicans have also voted to assert congressional authority over the US-Israel war with Iran.

If the Republican Party maintains control of both the House and Senate in November’s race, its majorities could continue to help Trump’s legislative agenda. But there is an important caveat.

Lawmakers will be keeping an anxious eye on voter sentiment as the 2028 elections approach. With Trump unable to seek a third term, some Republicans may have more appetite to publicly oppose the lame-duck president during the next two years, in order to boost their election prospects.

If Republicans maintain control of the Senate but lose the House, they would still be able to help Trump confirm his nominees for key federal roles.

Hundreds of federal positions require approval from a simple majority in the Senate, including roles in the judiciary, including Supreme Court justices.

The party in control of Congress, with a few exceptions, can determine what legislation is brought to a vote and when.

But for Democrats, the most significant outcome of winning a majority in one or both chambers would be the ability to block Trump from legislating his agenda over the next two years.

That said, analysts expect a Democrat-led Congress to take a largely defensive stance, batting down Trump’s proposals.

Going on offence — and passing their own legislative agenda — will be far more difficult, even if the party wins a majority in both the House and Senate. Democrat-led laws would still face Trump’s veto power.

However, holding majorities would help Democratic members slip policy priorities into “need-to-pass” funding legislation. The spectre of a government shutdown could pressure Republicans to pass budget bills, even if they do not agree on all the terms.

Democrats can also bring topics to a vote to force congressional Republicans to oppose popular policies or simply take a public stance on divisive issues.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has laid out a 100-day plan for if Democrats take control of the chamber. Topping the agenda are votes on Trump-backed healthcare funding cuts, asserting congressional authority over the US-Israel war with Iran and rolling back Trump’s tariff programme.

Those issues have split the Republican base and would pose thorny dilemmas for lawmakers already posturing for the 2028 vote.

As Trump rallies on behalf of Republicans in the run-up to November’s vote, he has repeatedly expressed concern that Democratic control of Congress could lead to one eventuality: his third impeachment.

Trump was already impeached twice during his first term. “If we don’t win, they’ll end up impeaching me,” he told a rally in Durant, Oklahoma, in early October.

If Democrats do take control of the House or the Senate, they will take over leadership of dozens of committees. Through those committees, they can launch investigations — with subpoena power — into an array of subjects.

Some Democrats have already said probing allegations of Trump family corruption will be a top priority.

House lawmakers can also introduce articles of impeachment and ultimately vote to impeach federal officials, including the president, with a simple majority.

However, the Senate would need to vote to convict the official with a two-thirds majority before they can be removed from office.

Perhaps more significantly, if Democrats win control of the Senate, they would be able to block the confirmation of Trump appointees in key roles during his final two years in office.

A Democratic surge is likely to signal discontent with the Trump administration, but there will not be a swift, tangible change on many of the issues that have defined the election season.

For example, if Democrats secure both majorities in Congress, they could assert their leverage to seek to address affordability issues, drilling into topics like housing, healthcare and the cost of living.

But they can do little to immediately change the myriad factors that led to the high price of petrol and groceries. Any gains would most likely be hard-fought, slow-coming and incremental.

The same is true for the US-Israel war with Iran.

Under the US Constitution, only Congress can declare war, something it has not done since World War II. Presidents have long used various legal arguments to circumvent that constitutional requirement.

Most recently, the Trump administration argued that the US-Israel war with Iran did not require authorisation from Congress because the president has a duty to protect the American people.

Trump has also argued that the war has started and stopped several times, each time renewing the 60-day window he has to receive Congress’s authorisation.

To reassert Congress’s authority to declare war, Democrats could pass a legally binding “war powers resolution” to rein in Trump, but they would need two-thirds support to overcome the presidential veto.

Even if a resolution were able to overcome the veto, experts say it is unclear how the US judiciary would respond if Trump were to flout Congress’s will.

Still, Democrats could use control of Congress to attempt to stifle any funding for the war.

news.originalContent:
The duo was first arrested for a suspected link to an incident at a US-run airbase used for striking Iran during this year’s war.

Police in the United Kingdom have re-arrested two men on suspicion of assisting Iran’s intelligence service after an incident at a United States-run airbase in England last month.

Counter Terrorism Policing in the UK said the men, a 24-year-old British national and a 25-year-old dual British-Iranian national, were arrested under the National Security Act.

One of the suspects was first arrested on September 27, when the suspected plot against RAF Fairford took place. The airbase in Gloucestershire in western England has been used to launch strikes on Iran during this year’s war.

The second suspect was first arrested on October 1. Until Tuesday, the men had been released on bail pending more investigation.

Below is State of the Day, a morning newsletter from the Daily Caller Editorial Desk. Sign up here.__________

Welcome to State of the Day,

Prepare yourselves; it’ll be a bloodbath for control,

The Conservative Establishment Is Planning For A Post-Trump GOP

More than 500 conservative officials, election administrators, policymakers, and civic leaders.

More than 30 gatherings across 20-plus states. And, for the most part, conversations happening behind closed doors.

That’s the picture Johns Hopkins University’s SNF Agora Institute and the R Street Institute painted in a report published this September, detailing three years of work to build what they call the “Civic Right” — a network of Republicans claiming to be focused on election trust, governing institutions, and the future of their movement.

The initiative’s organizers argue that conservatives need better infrastructure to connect leaders and turn their ideas into sustained political action.

Not exactly the most eye-catching stuff, but it offers a glimpse into the fight over what comes next for the Republican Party, a fight that is playing out beyond the boundaries of Washington’s catfights.

For some, the party’s future means doubling down on Donald Trump’s MAGA movement. For others, it means returning to the old guard of neoconservatism. And for others still, it means turning the page on both and looking for a new cause that’ll resonate with everyday Americans.

Amid all this, the mysterious Civic Right has been meeting privately to discuss what comes next.

The meetings aren’t exactly riveting. There are no stadium rallies, no viral clips, and no grand declaration of war against the current state of the Republican Party.

Instead, there’s an assortment of state officials, local political networks, policy groups, and grant money — the unsightly machinery that shapes politics before any of us even realize it.

The project is led by Scott Warren at Johns Hopkins’ SNF Agora Institute, with R Street’s Matt Germer among its authors. R Street president and co-founder Eli Lehrer came up through the Heritage Foundation, the American Enterprise Institute, and the Heartland Institute, and once wrote speeches for then-Senate Majority Leader Bill Frist.

In other words, this isn’t some grassroots revolt bubbling up from the ranks. It’s an organized effort by longtime center-right policy hands to build a network around their vision.

And there’s money behind the machinery, too. In June 2026, Carnegie Corporation of New York awarded Johns Hopkins $500,000 to support its Conservative Agenda for Democracy program.

Separately, public grant records show that R Street received millions in grants between 2018 and 2025, including $7.1 million from the William and Flora Hewlett Foundation, $2.4 million from the Pew Charitable Trusts, and $935,000 from the Charles Koch Institute.

Charles Koch’s funding network has supported open borders and foreign labor, drawing criticism from both sides of the aisle. In a 2015 interview with Vox, Sen. Bernie Sanders quipped, “Open borders? No, that’s a Koch brothers proposal.”

Sanders went on to correctly argue that businesses benefit from an expanded pool of workers willing to accept rock-bottom wages, which puts pressure on American workers and drives down pay; see cheap foreign labor.

And the Koch brothers aren’t alone. The William and Flora Hewlett Foundation, R Street’s largest reported funder, published a defense of expanded migration, arguing that greater opportunities to move abroad are among the fastest ways to raise living standards.

That’s just a taste of the sort of backers this venture boasts; take all the time you need to really breathe in that ripe swamp stench.

MAGA, on the other hand, offers a different vision, one built around Trump himself. His endorsements, feuds, and demands for loyalty have become defining features of the movement. The populist uprising that promised to take on the establishment has developed its own hierarchy, with Trump at the top.

But with Trump set to leave the presidency after 2028, the movement built around him faces its own identity crisis.

And don’t forget about the disaffected Republicans, as I like to call them, essentially the Thomas Massies and Marjorie Taylor Greenes of the world.

They’re conservatives who don’t neatly fit into either category, but are instead charting a path of their own. A mix of libertarian, conservative, and pragmatic policies makes up the third camp in the war for control.

Who’s to say who’ll come out on top?

The fight won’t just be about who’s the GOP nominee in ‘28; it’s about who has the money, networks, and local infrastructure to turn their vision of the Republican Party into reality.

While everyone argues over the future of the right, some are quietly building it.

How Jared And Ivanka Sparked A Revolution, Daily Caller, John Loftus

The Daily Caller’s John Loftus offers new reporting on the mounting backlash against Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump — along with their political allies in the Albanian government — over a private real estate deal to develop Sazan Island. Riots have broken out in the Albanian capital of Tiranë over what citizens see as a corrupt land deal that has given Kushner and Trump—along with partnered investors—control over the island.

Anthropic Floats Bill That Would Let Feds Step In Only When More Than 50 Lives Are On The Line, Daily Caller News Foundation, Dylan Kresak

Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic is lobbying Congress to back legislation that would ostensibly limit the Commerce Department’s regulatory oversight of the technology. The Artificial Intelligence Evaluation, Governance, and Incident Safety (AEGIS) Act would only allow federal regulators to step in and shut down an AI model once it has threatened to kill more than 50 people or cause over $1 billion in damage.

Putin Floats a Summit With Trump and Xi to Discuss Ukraine Deal, The Wall Street Journal, Lingling Wei, Alex Leary, Thomas Grove and Josh Dawsey

The Wall Street Journal reported that Vladimir Putin has floated a summit with President Trump and China’s Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The proposal comes as Washington and Beijing are embroiled in a race to lead the AI frontier. The plan could give Beijing a larger role in negotiations on European security, as Putin seeks to capitalize on warming ties with Trump.

Cattle Ranchers Are Getting Grilled 30 Days Into Trump’s Foreign Beef Blitz, Daily Caller, John Loftus

President Donald Trump’s decision to waive tariffs on beef imports from Argentina is costing American ranchers dearly. Just 30 days after the waiver was implemented, “prices paid for live and dressed cutter cows, which compete directly against the lean beef imports, have fallen 12.2 percent and 13.9 percent, respectively,” the watchdog group Farm Action reports. This price drop is significantly affecting American ranchers, who are already hard-pressed by rising diesel prices.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by NATHAN HOWARD/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Vice President J.D. Vance said Monday he would not endorse Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an interview with journalist Mark Halperin.

President Donald Trump offered Netanyahu his full endorsement Sunday ahead of Israel’s elections later this month.

“I endorse American candidates, and that’s where I’m focused on is the midterm,” Vance told Halperin aboard Air Force Two. “I’m not getting involved in Israeli elections.”

“I’m not anti-endorsing him. I’m not pro-endorsing him. I’m not getting involved in Israeli elections,” the vice president added.

Netanyahu is facing several challengers this election year, including Gadi Eisenkot, Yair Lapid, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, Yair Golan and Avigdor Liberman, all of whom are members of the opposition bloc. Recent polls show that Eisenkot and the Yashar party have a slight lead over Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party, but neither faction appears to have enough support yet to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset.

Trump on Sunday described the Israeli prime minister as a “Great Warrior and an even greater Partner for Peace in combatting [sic] the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

“If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself … This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much.”

During a recent interview with Fox News host Mark Levin, Netanyahu said that, if he wins re-election, his first goal would be to “achieve the complete elimination of the Iranian threat to Israel, to America, and to the world.” (RELATED: 45 Seconds Into Softball Interview, Netanyahu Tells Mark Levin He Wants To Drag The US Even Deeper Into Iran War)

“This is a regime that chants ‘death to Israel,’ ‘death to America’ — you’re the real target,” Netanyahu told Levin. “I think we are well on our way to achieving this with President Trump’s brilliant leadership, both militarily and then economic blockade, very effective. Let’s complete the job and have the people of Iran seize their own future. It changes the Middle East.”

Vance previously campaigned with Hungary’s then-prime minister, Viktor Orban, in Budapest days before the national election in April, which Orban lost. The vice president said he wanted “to help [Orban] in this campaign cycle” but that the U.S. would “work with whoever wins this election.”

محسن رضایی، دبیر شورای عالی امنیت ملی ایران، در دیدار با عاصم منیر، فرمانده کل نیروهای مسلح پاکستان، گفت: «ذره‌ای از مواد هسته‌ای غنی شده از ایران خارج نخواهد شد.» آقای منیر در این سفر، با مسعود پزشکیان، رئیس‌جمهور و محمدباقر قالیباف، رئیس مجلس ایران نیز دیدار کرد. در همین حال قیمت نفت که به بالاترین حد در پنج ماه گذشته رسیده بود به کمتر از ۱۱۰ دلار کاهش یافت.

خبرگزاری تسنیم، نزدیک به سپاه پاسداران، گزارش‌ها درباره سفر هیئتی از قطر به ایران را رد کرده و نوشته است:‌ «هیچ هیئتی از قطر به ایران سفر نکرده است.».

در چند روز گذشته تهران شاهد افزایش سفرهای دیپلماتیک از سوی رهبران منطقه بوده است. روز دوشنبه سرگئی لاوروف، وزیرخارجه روسیه برای نخستین بار بعد از جنگ اسرائیل و آمریکا با ایران به تهران رفت و ساعتی بعد از خروج او هم عاصم منیر، فرمانده ارتش پاکستان با مسعود پزشکیان، محمدباقر قالیباف و محسن رضایی دیدار و گفتگو کرد.

قطر و پاکستان از میانجیان فعال گفتگوها میان ایران و آمریکا در چند ماه گذشته بوده‌اند.

مسعود پزشکیان، رئیس جمهور ایران در دیدار با فیلد مارشال عاصم منیرگفت: «ما آماده گفتگو بوده و هستیم، اما آمریکایی‌ها باید اول تهدیدها و تحریم‌ها را بردارند و بعد گفتگو کنیم.»

سخنان آقای پزشکیان همسو با اظهارات محسن رضایی، دبیر شورای عالی امنیت ملی ایران است که روز سه‌شنبه در دیدار با عاصم منیر گفته بود برای آغاز مذاکره آمریکا باید با قبول شروط ایران اعتمادسازی کند.

آقای پزشکیان در دیدار خود با فرمانده ارتش پاکستان همچنین گفته است:‌ «ملت ما امروز به آمریکا اعتماد ندارد و معتقد است اگر مذاکره کنیم، دوباره به ما حمله خواهند کرد.»

سفر عاصم منیر، فرمانده پرنفوذ ارتش پاکستان که گفته می‌شود روابط خوبی هم با دونالد ترامپ دارد، یک روز پس از سفر سرگئی لاوروف، وزیرخارجه روسیه به تهران صورت گرفت و بسیاری آن را نشانی از افزایش رایزنی‌ها در منطقه با هدف پیشگیری از یک درگیری دیگر میان ایران و آمریکا ارزیابی کرده‌اند.

یک سخنگوی مرکز فرماندهی نیروهای ارتش آمریکا (سنتکام) به خبرگزاری الجزیره گفت که «ادعای ایران مبنی بر اصابت دو نفتکش با مین در تنگه هرمز صحت ندارد.»

به گزارش الجزیره این مقام نظامی افزود: «ما مسیرهای کشتیرانی بین‌المللی در تنگه هرمز را از مین پاکسازی کرده‌ایم. ایران در اقدامات تجاوزکارانه خود از موشک و پهپاد استفاده می‌کند.»

او همچنین تاکید کرده که بر خلاف گفته ایران، تنگه هرمز باز است و ۹۵ درصد کشتی‌ها «با موفقیت» از این آبراه عبور می‌کنند.

مسلم یعقوبی، معاون حقوقی ارتش ایران،‌ می‌گوید «فرض» بر این است که خلبانان مفقود ایرانی زنده هستند چون دلیلی برای کشته‌شدن آنها ارائه نشده است.

او در عین حال دولت قطر را به لحاظ حقوقی مسئول پاسخگویی درباره وضعیت این خلبانان دانست.

آقای یعقوبی با فرض زنده بودن این خلبانان گفت: «کشوری که میزبان اسیر است، مسئولیت زنده نگه داشتن، درمان، اطلاع‌رسانی به خانواده اسیران و تحویل آنان به مراجع دارای صلاحیت را برعهده دارد.»

معاون حقوقی ارتش می‌گوید که پس از جلساتی با وزارت خارجه و ستاد کل نیروهای مسلح و بررسی اطلاعات به این نتیجه رسیده که خلبانان ایرانی زنده هستند.

سرنوشت سه خلبان ایران همچنان در هاله‌ای از ابهام قرار دارد.

ایران می‌گوید دو جنگنده سوخو-۲۴ پس از حمله به مواضع آمریکا در قطر، در حال بازگشت به ایران بودند که هدف حمله قرار گرفتند.

چندی بعد ایران اعلام کرد که یکی از این خلبانان کشته و مراسم تدفین او برگزار شده است.

با این حال ستاد کل نیروهای مسلح اعلام کرد که سه خلبان دیگر زنده و در اسارت قطر هستند.

روز ۱۳ شهریور هلال احمر ایران خبر داد که از طریق صلیب سرخ پیگیر وضعیت این خلبانان شده است.

قطر همواره حضور این خلبانان در خاک خود را قاطعانه رد کرده و در مورد وضعیت آنها اظهار بی‌اطلاعی کرده است.

محسن رضایی، دبیر شورای عالی امنیت ملی ایران، در دیدار با عاصم منیر، فرمانده کل نیروهای مسلح پاکستان، گفت: «ذره‌ای از مواد هسته‌ای غنی شده از ایران خارج نخواهد شد.»

آقای رضایی همچنین گفت که پیش از اعتمادسازی آمریکا، مذاکره‌ای در کار نخواهد بود. او شروع این اعتمادسازی را تحقق شروط ایران دانست.

آقای منیر نیز تاکید کرد که مشکل مرزهای ایران و پاکستان برطرف شده و از امروز صبح تمام نقاط مرزی بین ایران و پاکستان بازگشایی شده است.

اشاره فرمانده ارتش پاکستان به اخبار و تصاویری است که در دو روز گذشته پیرامون بسته بودن مرز بین دو کشور منتشر شده است.

ساعاتی پیش اسماعیل بقایی، سخنگوی وزارت خارجه ایران، دلیل بسته شدن مرز را «مشکلات فنی» عنوان کرده بود.

فرمانده کل نیروهای مسلح پاکستان در این سفر، با مسعود پزشکیان، رئیس‌جمهور و محمدباقر قالیباف، رئیس مجلس ایران نیز دیدار کرده است.

یاشار گولر، وزیر دفاع ترکیه، می‌گوید که ترکیه تا زمانی که امنیت مرزهایش با سوریه و عراق به‌طور کامل تضمین نشود، نیروهای خود را در این دو کشور حفظ خواهد کرد.

آقای گولر به خبرگزاری فرانسه گفت: «ما حضور نظامی خود را در عراق و سوریه حفظ می‌کنیم.»

او افزود: «هرگاه ارزیابی کنیم که شرایط لازم از نظر امنیت منطقه‌ای و مرزی فراهم شده است، در مورد وضعیت پایگاه‌ها و حضورمان در منطقه تجدیدنظر خواهیم کرد.»

ترکیه سال‌هاست که برای مهار تهدید امنیت مرزهایش، نیروهایی را در شمال سوریه و عراق مستقر کرده است.

اما سقوط بشار اسد و روی کار آمدن دولت جدید سوریه از یک سو، و تلاش ترکیه برای پایان دادن به مناقشه چند ده ساله‌اش با حزب پ‌ک‌ک، وضعیت تغییر کرده است.

آقای گولر گفت که پس از سقوط حکومت بشار اسد، ترکیه «هماهنگی نزدیکی در حوزه امنیتی» با دولت جدید سوریه برقرار کرده و نیروهای ترکیه در حال تلاش برای «تقویت توانمندی» ارتش سوریه و «تضمین امنیت مرزهای ما» هستند.

او گفت: «زمانی که تهدید تروریستی در منطقه به‌طور کامل از بین برود، امنیت مرزها تضمین شود و اقتدار دولت مرکزی به‌طور کامل و یکپارچه در سراسر سوریه برقرار گردد، در مورد وضعیت نیروهایمان بازنگری خواهیم کرد.»

پلیس مبارزه با تروریسم بریتانیا دو مردی که در پی حادثه‌ امنیتی پایگاه هوایی فرفورد بازداشت‌ شده بودند را دوباره دستگیر کرده است.

به گفته پلیس، یک تبعه بریتانیایی ۲۴ ساله و یک فرد ۲۵ ساله با تابعیت دوگانه بریتانیایی-ایرانی، به ظن همکاری با یک سرویس اطلاعاتی خارجی هم اکنون در بازداشت به سر می‌برند.

لارنس تیلور، دستیار کمیسر و رئیس پلیس ملی مبارزه با تروریسم، گفت: «این تحقیقات در جریان است و روند گردآوری شواهد همچنان ادامه دارد؛ اما در حال حاضر موضع ما تغییری نکرده است؛ ما احتمال می‌دهیم که دولت ایران در این ماجرا نقش داشته باشد.»

او فزود: «بازرسان ما همچنان در حال بررسی ابعاد این دخالت و اهداف پشت‌پردهٔ آن هستند.»

در پی این حادثه که در ساعات اولیه روز ۲۷ سپتامبر (۵ مهر) رخ داد، بسیاری از مقام‌های بریتانیا از جمله اندی برنام،‌ نخست‌وزیر و کن مک‌کالم، رئیس ام‌آی۵ (سازمان اطلاعات داخلی بریتانیا) حکومت ایران و سپاه پاسداران را متهم به ارتباط با این حادثه کردند.

پس از این اتهام ایران و بریتانیا سفرای یکدیگر را احضار کرده و مراتب اعتراض خود را ابلاغ کردند.

دو نفر در ارتباط با حادثه پایگاه فرفورد به ظن کمک به سرویس اطلاعاتی ایران دوباره بازداشت شدند

یک مقام قضایی لبنان گفت که یک قاضی این کشور امروز دستور داد تا دو عضو حزب‌الله برای بازجویی درباره دست داشتن احتمالی‌شان در انتقال محموله‌ای از مواد منفجره که مقام‌های لبنانی اخیرا توقیف کرده‌ بودند، حاضر شوند.

بر اساس گزارش خبرگزاری فرانسه، مقام‌های لبنان پس از بازداشت دو فرد مظنون به عضویت در حزب‌الله که متهم‌ شدند در حال حمل نیم تن مواد منفجره بودند، تحقیقاتی در این باره شروع کردند.

حزب‌الله که از حمایت ایران برخوردار است اعلام کرد که این مواد بخشی از «توانمندی‌های» این گروه برای استفاده علیه اسرائیل بوده است.

این دو متهم  ۸ اکتبر در یک ایست بازرسی امنیتی در شرق لبنان و در اتومبیلی که به سمت بیروت در حرکت بود، بازداشت شدند.

یک منبع به خبرگزاری فرانسه گفت یکی از آنها پسر یکی از مقام‌های حزب‌الله و دیگری هم از اعضای این گروه است.

نفت در معاملات پرنوسان روز سه‌شنبه، از نزدیک به ۱۱۲ دلار در هر بشکه به پایین‌تر از ۱۱۰ دلار افت کرد.
قراردادهای آتی نفت خام برنت صبح به وقت شرق آمریکا با ۶۷ سنت کاهش به ۱۰۸/۸۸ دلار در هر بشکه رسید اما پیش از آن تا ۱۱۱/۹۹ دلار بالا رفته بود که بالاترین در پنج ماه گذشته محسوب می‌شد.

رسانه‌های و چهره‌های محافظه‌کار و تندرو در ایران سفر عاصم منیر را به کاهش قیمت نفت ربط داده‌اند.

ابراهیم رضایی عضو کمیسیون امنیت ملی مجلس در ایکس نوشت: «میانجی که دائما علیه ایران موضع می‌گیرد و ما را مقصر جنگ چهل‌ روزه معرفی می‌کند، پول مردم ایران را (به دستور دشمن ایران) بلوکه کرده است، راه‌بندان می‌کند یا عامل عملیات خشم اقتصادی علیه ایرانیان می‌شود و در آخر، وقتی فشار به آمریکا مضاعف می‌گردد، پیدایش می‌شود، میانجی نیست، بخشی از ماشین جنگ ترکیبی دشمن است؛ مراقب باشید.»

خبرگزاری فارس که به نهادهای امنیتی و نظامی نزدیک است نوشت: «با سفر عاصم منیر، فرمانده ارتش پاکستان و میانجی مذاکرات ایران و آمریکا به تهران، بار دیگر موضوع احیای مذاکرات در کانون توجه رسانه‌ها و چهره‌های جریان اصلاح‌طلب قرار گرفته است؛ رویکردی که در ماه‌های گذشته نیز با انتشار هر خبر تازه از تحرک میانجی‌ها و احتمال ازسرگیری گفت‌وگوها در تیترهای این رسانه‌ها بازتاب یافته است.»

به گزارش رسانه‌های ایران، این اولین دیدار فرمانده کل قوای پاکستان با عباس عراقچی خواهد بود.

علاوه بر این، اینکه محسن رضایی درخواست ملاقات عاصم منیر را رد کرده است تکذیب شد.

ایران  در نامه‌ای به سازمان ملل متحد تهدید آمریکا به استفاده از مادر بمب‌ها را محکوم کرده و خواستار توقف تهدیدهای این کشور و اسرائیل شده است.

این نامه با امضای غلامحسین درزی، سفیر و کاردار جمهوری اسلامی ایران در مقر سازمان ملل متحد در نیویورک، خطاب به دبیرکل و رئیس دوره‌ای شورای امنیت صادر شده است.

نماینده ایران در این نامه از این دو مقام خواسته است «فوری از ایالات متحده و رژیم اسرائیل بخواهند که به تهدیدهای غیرقانونی خود پایان دهند و به‌طور کامل به تعهداتشان ذیل منشور ملل متحد و قواعد آمره حقوق بین‌الملل پایبند باشند.»

شبکه خبری سی‌ان‌ان هفته پیش به نقل از چند مقام آمریکایی گزارش داد که ارتش آن کشور طرح‌های تازه‌ای برای حمله به ایران تهیه کرده است که استفاده احتمالی از بمب موسوم به «مادر همه بمب‌ها» را هم شامل می‌شود و در صورتی که دونالد ترامپ دستور ازسرگیری عملیات نظامی را  صادر کند، استفاده از چنین بمبی از گزینه‌های مطرح است.

مسعود پزشکیان، رئیس‌جمهور ایران، با حکمی مجید ابن‌الرضا را به عنوان مشاورش در امور دفاعی منصوب کرد.

در پی کشته‌شدن عزیز نصیرزاده، وزیر پیشین دفاع ایران در حمله ۹ اسفند ۱۴۰۴، مجید ابن‌الرضا «سرپرست» این وزارتخانه شد.

این سرپرستی یکشنبه با رای اعتماد مجلس به مهرداد اخلاقی به عنوان وزیر جدید دفاع به پایان رسید.

آقای ابن‌الرضا پیش از سرپرستی وزارت دفاع، در مرداد ۱۴۰۴ با پیشنهاد آقای نصیرزاده و تایید علی خامنه‌ای، رهبر وقت جمهوری اسلامی، به‌عنوان جانشین وزیر دفاع منصوب شده بود.

سازمان ملل روز سه‌شنبه اعلام کرد که تاکنون بیش از ۲۵۰ هزار نفر از درگیری‌های تازه در یمن گریخته‌اند.

این سازمان با ابراز نگرانی از وضعیت کسانی که در شهر تعز و حومه آن پناه گرفته‌اند، هشدار داد که دسترسی به این مناطق «عملا مسدود» شده است.

فولکر تورک، کمیسر عالی حقوق بشر سازمان ملل، می‌گوید که حوثی‌ها با بستن تنها مسیر تعز به عدن، مانع رسیدن کمک‌های بشردوستانه و دسترسی به اقلام ضروری شده و غیرنظامیان را در معرض خطری جدی قرار داده‌اند.

او از حوثی‌ها خواست که فورا اجازه دهند کمک‌ها وارد تعز شوند.

آقای تورک یادآور شد که کشته شدن ۳۲ غیرنظامی، از جمله ۱۴ کودک و ۹ زن، در سراسر این استان تایید شده است.

او تاکید کرد که وضعیت در تعز به‌ویژه نگران‌کننده است، زیرا حدود نیمی از کسانی که اخیرا بر اثر خشونت‌ها بی‌جا شده‌اند، در این شهر پناه گرفته‌اند.

سازمان عملیات تجاری بریتانیا می‌گوید گزارشی از وقوع یک حادثه‌ در آبهای نزدیک عمان دریافت کرده است که یک نفتکش و نیروهای نظامی در آن دخیل بوده‌اند.

به گزارش این نهاد ناظر وابسته به نیروی دریایی بریتانیا، این نفتکش در فاصله ۱۲۱ مایل دریایی از شرق بندر دقم عمان، تحت تاثیر عملیات نظامی در منطقه قرار گرفت.

بر اساس بیانیه این نهاد، مقامات در حال تحقیق درباره این حادثه هستند.

پیشتر سپاه پاسداران در بیانیه‌ای اعلام کرده بود که دو نفتکش «متخلف» در تنگه هرمز بر اثر انفجار مین «به آتش کشیده و متوقف شده‌اند.»
